title: Module sheafification commutes with continuous cocontinuous restriction
statement: Let $F:(C,J)\to(D,K)$ be continuous and cocontinuous between small sites, and let $R$ be a ring sheaf on $D$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be restriction on module presheaves and module sheaves respectively, and let $S$ and $S^\prime$ be module sheafification on $D$ and $C$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is a natural isomorphism $S^\prime P\simeq Q S$ taking the source sheafification-unit image of $x\in M(F(X))$ to its original unit image over $F(X)$. The functor $Q$ is additive. Maps from $Q S(M)$ to a module sheaf are equal if they agree on these original unit sections on any locally exhaustive covering locus of $C$.

source.place: Tag 04B8, lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification; slice application Tag 04IY, sites-modules-lemma-relocalize

proof.text: Restrict the sheafification unit and transpose it under source-site module sheafification. The restricted unit is locally bijective because F is cocontinuous. Hence its sheafification is invertible, and the adjoint transpose is that invertible map followed by the invertible counit. Unit naturality proves naturality; the adjunction inverse equation gives the unit formula. Precompose with this comparison and use covering-locus hom-ext to test maps from a restricted sheafification on original unit sections.
